chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Ja'far from his fathers (peace be upon them) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The charity of a loaf of bread is better than a lean sacrificial animal.' And whoever buys his sacrificial animal as fat, and finds it so, or finds it lean, he has fulfilled his obligation; and if he buys it lean with knowledge of that, he has not fulfilled his obligation. It was narrated.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim buys a lean sacrificial animal for Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between unintentional defect (jahalah) and intentional deficiency (ikhtiyar) in the sacrificial animal (hady), affirming validity in the former but not the latter. It pairs this legal precision with a prophetic maxim emphasizing that sincere, simple charity holds greater spiritual weight than a ritual sacrifice performed with negligence or lack of devotion. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the internal state of the worshipper alongside the external validity of the act.
